front: What are the defining characteristics of a set?
back: A set is unordered, holds only unique values and is mutable. Adding a duplicate changes nothing, and the elements must be hashable (immutable) values.

front: How do you create an empty set, and why not `{}`?
back: Use `set()`. Empty curly braces `{}` create an empty dictionary. A populated set is written `{1, 2, 3}`.
The set drops the duplicates, so only three unique colours remain. Sorting gives a predictable order to print.
Sets have no positions, so there are no indexes and no slices. Use `in` to ask whether a value is present.

code:
seen = {1, 2}
seen.add(3)
seen.add(3)
seen.discard(10)
seen.remove(1)
print(sorted(seen), 1 not in seen)
back: `add()` inserts a value, `remove()` deletes it and raises `KeyError` if it is missing, and `discard()` deletes it silently. `not in` tests absence.
